questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was very important that the university had courses that were interesting and also maybe had some courses that we are not able to take at KU. I also wanted to be in an English speaking country, so I chose based country based on that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest to find information before arrival. They did not start to send out emails about orientation and such until very close to the start of the semester, which was a bit confusing when you are moving to a different country. Also, there were some problems with the coordinater and her emails not being sent to everyone but only some people got them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had both social and academic orientation, which was really great and informing!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest to find housing outside off campus, since there is a housing shortage in all of Ireland at the moment. On places like Facebook there are also a lot of scammers, so it is hard to find something good. I was lucky to find accommodation on Facebook through a group dedicated to students at UCC, but usually Facebook is not your best option.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The students in Cork usually live in houses with many living together, usually 5-8 people in one house. Living in one of these houses is a great way to become friends with the locals!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky to find my own accommodation, but there really is not a lot of housing available for studnets in Cork in general. The university claims they can help you find housing but you have to wait a long time or they cannot find anything for you. My advice is to look for housing early in the process, even before you get fully accepted to the university, just to be sure you don't have to pay too much for housing or end up with a place very far away.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process is pretty straight forward, but you get accepted to the university very late, which is a bit of an annoyance if you want to wait with booking housing and such.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to log into a portal, that takes you through the process. You have to upload different documents and such.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the international office for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Because you have to take about 6 courses at UCC, it can be pretty hard to get all the courses you want since they are not allowed to overlap with their schedules. I ended up with interesting courses, but some were not my first choice. With many of the classes, you have to get approved by the department to be allowed to take the classes, and this can unfortunately take a while, which is annoying cause if you get rejected for a class, you have to register for another and also wait for approving here. The decision from the department is final and it is often not stated what the decision is based on, which can be frustration. I find this system really strange and it adds stress in the beginning of the semester which is very unnecessary and avoidable if courses were chosen earlier.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to write to the international office for help, since the process can be really confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of my courses to the a little lower than what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At UCC there was mostly just lectures and no classes for working with the lecture material and such, which we have at UCPH in most of my courses.
Generally they also went into less details in the courses, but this was probably because the courses were only 5ECTS points each.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Cell Biology - BC4001
Cell and Molecular Basis of Neurodegenerative Disease - BC4011
Developmental Genetics - GN4001
Introduction to Modern Irish History for Visiting Students - HI1115
Virology - MB3022
Chemotherapy and Pharmacology of Inflammation - PT2101

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Cell and Molecular Basis of Neurodegenerative Disease, very interesting course! 
The others were not bad, but they just were not at the level we are used to in Copenhagen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Alcohol can be more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport around town with the bus was very cheap with a student travel card! Also you save money on a gym membership since the gym is free for the university students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a ton of clubs and sports to join at the university, and it was a great opportunity to meet locals and also other international people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, the international office arranged different events so we could meet other students. There are also arranged trips to different parts of ireland. I also really enjoyed watching the school rugby team play games every Saturday.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the free gym and go to pubs like a true irish person

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes with the Mountaineering club, they go every sunday to a new place! It's a great way to meet other international students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was pretty easy to adjust to the culture. It is not too different to Denmark, you just have to get used to everything being in English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs/sports and talk to the people in your courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Really no differences stood out to me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the irish people are some of the nicest ever, and they are great to just bring you to places or just include you in their friend group!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to not get your first priority of courses. Be patient with the registration and international office, everything will work out in the end. Start looking for housing early!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Befriend someone local, so they can keep you up to date with the unwritten "party" days like freshers week, college Christmas Day and such

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved living with 4 irish girls and it really made my experience better by being brought into their world and friend group.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lack of structure in the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Cork for the people and the nature of ireland, not for the academics

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
